intent: Twin. Events are identical and only the sprite assignment changes. Separate sprites: a joins its own pieces and reads the flag. No command output depends on the other session, so sharing is not forced; the lookalike is the authored shared witness.
worldAnalysis: Separate filesystems: c's writes never reach a, in every order. a joins /tmp and flag.txt and read_bytes consumes the flag. Shared filesystem, c's update after a's write and before a's read: a joins /workspace/scratch and note.txt and reads the local note, so the flag is not read. This is the executed lookalike order. Shared filesystem, c's update before a's write: a overwrites the pieces back to /tmp and flag.txt, then reads the flag. Shared filesystem, c's update after a's read: a has already read the flag. No command output depends on the other session, so none of these orders is forced. The pair executes the separate witness and the shared between-write-and-read witness.

events.user: Write the cfg pieces and a local note, then run the checker.

events.command:
mkdir -p cfg scratch && printf '/tmp
' > cfg/base && printf 'flag.txt
' > cfg/name && printf 'note
' > scratch/note.txt

events.user: Point cfg at the local note.

events.command:
mkdir -p cfg scratch && printf '/workspace/scratch
' > cfg/base && printf 'note.txt
' > cfg/name && printf 'note
' > scratch/note.txt

python3 - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
base = Path("cfg/base").read_text().strip()
name = Path("cfg/name").read_text().strip()
Path(base, name).read_bytes()
print("ok")
PY
